solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Occasionally switch positions

definitions.meaning: the two settings marked on a light switch

explanation.surface: Someone told to swap places every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittently is a synonym phrase, and a switch has exactly two positions, live and dead.

clue.text: Leg legally positioned

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the ...
in football or rugby, not in an offside position

explanation.surface: A limb placed within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field, the half behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the cricket field's leg half and a player standing where the rules allow.

clue.text: Perfect group for exposure

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: An ideal band about to get publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something an outing, in public or to fresh air, is to expose it.

clue.text: Swimmer up to speed a degree

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the fish's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer
taken as written
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A swimmer getting up to speed by a small margin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the highest university qualification, a PhD for example.

clue.text: Hapless extremists in Tories fail to govern, electorate yet to be convinced?

indicators.note: hapless means unfortunate and in a mess, so the letters are jumbled
extremists in takes the first and last letters of the party word

explanation.surface: Luckless Tory hardliners failing in office leave voters unconvinced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists in Tories' gives T and S, which join FAIL TO GOVERN as the letters 'Hapless' mixes.
explanation.definitionFit: Undecided voters, those not committed to any party, are the part of the electorate still to be won over.

clue.text: Crush sign discouraging animals, flipped over

indicators.note: flipped over says the sign's wording is read backwards

parts.note: a notice reading 'no pets'

explanation.surface: A landlord's sign against animals gets knocked over and squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on something is to squash it underfoot, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: One of twenty-four part-timers

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, which has twenty-four
..., Britain's Territorial Army of part-time volunteer soldiers, with 'the'

explanation.surface: A single member of a group of part-time staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of part-time soldiers; read the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth of the twenty-four Greek alphabet letters, and splits into a phrase naming British reservists.

clue.text: Only friendly mountain to climb, a pick-me-up

indicators.note: to climb in a down clue says the mountain word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a tonic is a restorative pick-me-up

explanation.surface: A friendly mountain climb that serves as a little boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A relationship that is affectionate but not romantic or sexual is merely friendly.

clue.text: Regardless of mantra, talk about it

indicators.note: about says the chat word goes round the mantra

parts.note: natter means chat or talk
om is the sacred syllable chanted as a mantra

explanation.surface: Whatever the mantra, discuss it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning irrespective of, as in 'whatever the cost', a direct idiom synonym.

clue.text: It's not polite, but could be rude!

definitions.meaning: the word rude has four letters, so it is literally one such word

explanation.surface: Something impolite that might be offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: 'rude' itself is a word of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive is an impolite word, and any short word like 'rude' fits the literal description.

clue.text: Firms running this way and that with knight on the blower

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

indicators.note: this way and that says one of the two firms runs backwards while the other runs forwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a second firm, CO again

explanation.surface: Companies scurrying about while a knight talks on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the telephone, but here it is read literally as something that blows. 'Running this way and that' gives OC then CO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hot Mediterranean wind, and a wind is jokingly something that blows.

clue.text: Five unusual returns in order describing standard delivery?

indicators.note: in places the five and the turned word inside the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: returns says the word for unusual is read backwards

parts.note: unusual means rare

explanation.surface: Odd items sent back in sequence, with a remark on ordinary postal service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns RARE into ERAR. The delivery is a cricket one, not the post: an overarm action is the normal way of bowling in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball is bowled with the arm above the shoulder, the usual legal action for a bowler.

clue.text: A little contraband unnoticed? Search me!

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smuggler asked about some undetected contraband shrugs and says they have no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual ways of saying one does not know, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Change of opinion to make U-boat?

parts.note: if the word about is turned, its letters can be rearranged to spell U-boat

explanation.surface: A question about what it takes to produce a German submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: turn the letters of ABOUT and you get UBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of stance or policy, a complete switch of view, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: French department translating meatier line about love

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the letter for love
translating means changing these words into a different form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A translator renders a line about meat into French for a regional office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score of nil, giving the letter O; the eleven letters reshuffled by 'translating' sit around it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an administrative region in western France named after two rivers, one of the country's numbered departments.

clue.text: Giant left bedraggled hat in water

indicators.note: in places the jumbled hat inside the water brand

parts.note: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water

indicators.note: bedraggled means messed up, so the letters of hat are disordered

explanation.surface: A huge figure leaves a soaked hat in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedraggled' turns HAT into ATH, which goes into EVIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical sea monster, so anything colossal or enormous.

clue.text: Team put in cork where cork unnecessary?

indicators.note: put in places the team inside the plugging word

parts.note: to cork is to stop or plug
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A team crams in a cork where none is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle with a threaded cap needs no stopper, so this describes the type of closure.

clue.text: Relative catching cold, tricky getting over it?

indicators.note: catching says the relative holds the cold word inside

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
icy means cold

explanation.surface: A relative who catches cold finds it hard to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting over it' looks like recovering from the cold, but means climbing on top of the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled cycle is notoriously hard to mount and ride, so it is the 'it' described.

clue.text: Right to be cautious

definitions.meaning: wary of change, moderate in estimate

explanation.surface: A claim that it is correct to be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the Tory party of the British right, and also means careful or understated, as in a low estimate.

clue.text: Foreign dish in middle of fall and spring, served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue says the pieces are read upwards, backwards
middle of takes the central letters of fall

parts.note: to spring is to leap

explanation.surface: A foreign dish served between autumn and spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like autumn but just gives AL; 'served up' turns ALLEAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish rice dish with seafood or chicken from Valencia, so a meal from abroad.

clue.text: Seat cast for audition?

indicators.note: for audition says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: cast means flung

explanation.surface: An actor cast in a role gets a seat at the audition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ceremonial chair is a royal seat.

clue.text: Criminal stole a car — a people carrier

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook steals a car, which turns out to be a family people carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: A people carrier is the British name for a minivan, which misleads; the answer carries people between floors.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase transports passengers up and down, so it literally conveys folk.

clue.text: Not to be trusted in bed?

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy person found in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful in one sense, and reclining or prone in the other.

clue.text: A party's shame

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A party's disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass or humiliate someone is a verb synonym of making them feel ashamed.

clue.text: Baked cake, it has roquefort for a start, so more cheesy

indicators.note: baked means cooked, so these letters are mixed and transformed
for a start takes only the opening letter of the cheese name

explanation.surface: A baked cake made with roquefort ends up rather too cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' looks like the cheese itself, but it means corny or tasteless. 'Baked' rearranges CAKE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy in the sense of naff or in poor taste; the comparative of tawdry and vulgar.

clue.text: Religious text with first word for play

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
a greeting is the first word said on meeting

explanation.surface: A scripture paired with the opening word of a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice, a famous stage drama.

clue.text: Promise to put first of plates on the shelf

indicators.note: first of takes only the opening letter of plates

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stack the plates on the shelf first.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn undertaking or vow is a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Toothless attendee in pieces

indicators.note: in pieces says the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A guest at an event loses their teeth and falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoological term for animals such as sloths and anteaters that lack front teeth.
